kf: UK teledermatology is mostly **store-and-forward**: advice and guidance, or images on all **suspected-cancer skin referrals**.
Image standard: **three views**: regional (where), close-up with ruler, and **dermoscopic**.
Good images let specialists triage, reassure or fast-track and avoid wasted appointments.
Pitfalls: poor focus, glare, no scale, wrong lesion, missing history; images can't be palpated.
Consent, secure systems and record-keeping are required.
myths: **"Photos replace examination"**: they support triage; full-skin checks still matter.
patho_lead: Teledermatology works by **sending the right images and history** to the right specialist.

mech.t: Trained staff take standard regional, close-up and dermoscopic images.
Images and history go through a secure NHS system.
Specialist decides: reassure, treat in primary care, routine or urgent clinic.
Some services add AI risk scoring (NICE HTG746).

comp: Missed diagnosis from poor images; information governance breaches.
